facts.text: Lancaster, New Hampshire, takes its name from Lancaster in England, echoing the settlers’ heritage.
Weeks Memorial Library, a Beaux Arts landmark listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2000, was donated by John W. Weeks.
Lancaster sits along the Connecticut River, serves as Coös County’s seat, and is the gateway to the Great North Woods Region.
The clever, caring, independent fox has long symbolized Lancaster, appearing in local lore and community events for over a century.
An extension of the Boston, Concord & Montreal Railroad once shipped products and tourists, while a Maine Central line skirted the Connecticut River.
Part of the White Mountain National Forest lies in Lancaster, and Senator John W. Weeks helped create the forest through congressional legislation.
